name: Space Needle
headline: height
subtitle: Observation tower at Seattle Center, Washington
description: The Space Needle is an observation tower in Seattle built for the 1962 World's Fair, where it opened on 21 April 1962 after roughly 400 days of construction. Its slender legs carry a saucer-shaped top house with an observation deck at 520 ft, and the aircraft warning beacon on top reaches 605 ft above the ground. It stands on a 120 by 120 ft lot, anchored to a concrete foundation 30 ft deep.

facts.text: It took 467 cement trucks less than 12 hours to fill the foundation hole, at the time the largest continuous concrete pour attempted in the West.
The tower is fastened to its foundation with 72 bolts, each 30 ft long, and its centre of gravity is only 5 ft above the ground.
The two high-speed elevators travel at 10 mph (800 ft per minute) and reach the top house in 43 seconds.
Built in about 400 days, it was nicknamed the '400-day wonder'.

caveats: The official fact sheets give weights in 'tons' without saying short or metric (the needle structure 3,700 tons and the foundation 5,850 tons), and the current fact page leaves the weight blank, so no mass is stored.
The halo diameter, foundation and elevator figures come from a 2016 archived copy of the official fun-facts page, before the 2018 renovation; they may not reflect later changes.
